title: Very Hot Drinks Could Increase Cancer Risk
paragraphs: Many people enjoy their tea or coffee very hot. However, a large new study from the UK suggests that drinking very hot drinks may increase the risk of a type of cancer in the esophagus, the tube that carries food from the mouth to the stomach.

The study was published in the International Journal of Cancer in 2026. The researchers used information on nearly one million adults from two large UK studies, the Million Women Study and the UK Biobank. The participants were followed for up to 14 years. During this time, 2,348 people developed cancer of the esophagus.
The participants had answered questions about how many hot drinks they had each day and how hot they liked them. They could choose from cold, warm, hot or very hot.

The researchers looked at two main types of cancer of the esophagus. For one type, called squamous cell carcinoma, the results were clear. People who liked their drinks very hot had more than three times the risk of people who liked them warm. Also, people who had six or more hot drinks a day had a 71% higher risk than people who had fewer. However, the temperature of drinks did not seem to affect the risk of the other main type of cancer.
The researchers estimated that about 14% of cases of squamous cell carcinoma in the UK could be prevented if people who drink very hot drinks let them cool down a little.

However, the study had some limitations. The participants reported the temperature of their drinks themselves, and people have different ideas about what "very hot" means. Also, the study only shows a link, not a cause.
Experts point out that smoking and drinking a lot of alcohol are among the better-known risk factors for this type of cancer.
